sources.text: Lançamentos de games em NOVEMBRO de 2026 - Calendário VOXL Além do aguardado GTA 6, novembro traz remake de Ocarina of Time e mais de 30 jogos. Confira as estreias do mês. Crédito: Voxl A Rockstar Games anunciou nesta segunda-feira (9) a realização do Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival , evento musical especial inspirado no universo de GTA 6. O festival acontecerá no dia 21 de novembro de 2026 , no espaço Mana Wynwood, em Miami, nos Estados Unidos, e contará com apresentações de artistas como Travis Scott, Cardi B, Justice e Metro Boomin. O evento foi organizado para celebrar o lançamento de Grand Theft Auto VI e reunirá músicos presentes no jogo e em sua trilha sonora oficial. A programação terá dois palcos com apresentações ao longo do festival, incluindo shows e sets de DJs. A iniciativa é uma parceria entre Rockstar Games e PlayStation, com produção dos responsáveis pelo festival III Points. A entrada será permitida apenas para maiores de 17 anos, e os ingressos serão distribuídos por meio de um sorteio, com inscrições abertas no site oficial do evento. A programação do Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival reúne nomes de diferentes estilos musicais, passando pelo hip-hop, música eletrônica e ritmos latinos, seguindo os padrões das rádios do game . Um dos destaques será a apresentação especial da Cactus Jack, gravadora e selo musical de Travis Scott, que também contará com Don Toliver, Kodak Black e Sofaygo. Confira a lista completa de artistas confirmados: A seleção reforça a importância da música na identidade de GTA 6, que terá Vice City como um dos principais cenários. A trilha sonora é uma parte tradicional da franquia, com estações de rádio, músicas licenciadas e artistas que ajudam a construir a personalidade de cada cidade. Os ingressos para o evento serão vendidos por meio de uma loteria organizada pela plataforma DICE, com códigos exclusivos enviados pelo serviço Laylo. Os interessados precisam se inscrever no sorteio pelo site oficial do festival . O prazo para participar termina em 10 de novembro, às 16h (horário de Brasília). Os vencedores serão anunciados no mesmo dia, às 19h (horário de Brasília), enquanto a venda dos ingressos para os selecionados começa em 11 de novembro, às 14h (horário de Brasília). Cada comprador poderá adquirir até dois ingressos, que não poderão ser transferidos para outras pessoas. A organização também recomenda criar uma conta na DICE utilizando o mesmo e-mail e telefone informados durante a inscrição na loteria, evitando que a participação seja identificada como atividade de bots. O Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival acontecerá no Mana Wynwood, localizado no endereço 318 NW 23rd St, em Miami. A organização recomenda utilizar serviços de transporte por aplicativo, já que o espaço não terá estacionamento próprio e as vagas disponíveis nas proximidades serão administradas por terceiros. Além da exigência de idade mínima de 17 anos, o evento terá regras específicas de segurança e acesso. Todos os participantes passarão por revistas, incluindo inspeção de bolsas e pertences pessoais, e não será permitida a entrada com alimentos, bebidas, armas, drones ou equipamentos profissionais de gravação. A organização também divulgou orientações de acessibilidade, incluindo áreas reservadas para pessoas com deficiência e a possibilidade de solicitar pulseiras especiais gratuitamente no local. O espaço contará com rotas acessíveis entre entradas, palcos e demais áreas do festival. O festival acontece próximo ao lançamento de Grand Theft Auto VI, que chega em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series S e X. O novo jogo da Rockstar acompanha a história de Jason e Lucia em Leonida, estado fictício inspirado na Flórida, com Vice City como principal cidade. A música terá papel importante na construção desse universo, seguindo a tradição da franquia de misturar artistas conhecidos, estações de rádio e composições licenciadas. O festival em Miami amplia essa proposta para além dos videogames, levando parte da identidade musical de GTA 6 para um evento presencial. Além do festival, a Rockstar também já anunciou outras iniciativas em parceria com o mundo da música. A empresa lançará um álbum em CD e vinil com músicas da trilha sonora de GTA 6 , além de produzir uma série de faixas com o duo Justice exclusivamente para o game . A empresa também está levando o jogo para o mundo real em diversas ações de marketing, mostrando que GTA VI promete ir além do mercado de games. A companhia deu vida aos restaurantes da franquia em Miami e levará a temática de Vice City para uma partida de basquete no lançamento do jogo. E aí, você está ansioso para jogar GTA 6? sources.text: How far would you travel to make it to the GTA 6 festival? Just when you thought the celebrations for Grand Theft Auto 6 couldn't get any more extravagant, Rockstar has announced that it will be hosting a huge music festival in Miami just a few days after its release. But that begs the question: who's going to turn up? I thought everyone was going to be playing GTA 6 ? "Experience the music of Vice City and Leonida at Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a special live event on November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami to celebrate the launch of GTAVI, featuring a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack," an official blog post reads. The event is in partnership with PlayStation and will feature "two stages of nonstop music performances" with the following artists: Tickets will be available via a lottery system for those aged 17+ with exclusive codes being sent out to those who managed to win a spot when the entries are drawn on today at 4 pm ET/ 9 pm GMT. But there are a couple things to keep in mind. There's no word on how expensive the tickets will be, with prices likely being revealed later today in the lottery, and the festival is a mere two weeks away, as it takes place on November 21, 2026. So, unless you're a super fan with money to spare on not only a festival ticket but also a last-minute plane ticket to Miami, this event will likely be for locals or, at the very least, those already in the US. My only issue is that if you're so big a fan that you're willing to drop everything last minute and head over to Florida then why aren't you actually playing GTA 6? The festival is happening just two days after GTA 6, I'm pretty sure we're all busy around then. sources.title: GTA 6 Caused Some Gamers to Hold Off on Buying New Games — Including Take-Two's Own NBA 2K27, Strauss Zelnick Says
sources.text: The behemoth that is GTA 6 looms large over the video game industry, and it’s so big that it not only caused the September crush of releases, but caused some gamers to hold off on buying new games. Reporting its latest financial results, Take-Two, parent company of GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games, said that its own NBA 2K27 had sold 4 million units, which was “below our forecast for the period.” Take-Two, which owns both 2K and NBA developer Visual Concepts, said that the NBA 2K27 launch window was “unusually busy, with numerous entertainment experiences competing for players’ attention.” In an accompanying interview with IGN , Zelnick expanded on the point, adding that he felt that GTA 6 had an impact also. “I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. It's an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. And in launching more content than ever before for the rest of the year, we have expectations that the title will do even better than it already has done,” Zelnick began. “I do think that this timing may have affected performance so far. It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer. That said, we're thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.” GTA 6 is credited with forcing developers and publishers to either bring their releases forward or move them back in an effort to avoid November. The likes of The Blood of Dawn Walker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel's Wolverine, Control Resonant and others all launched up against each other in September. NBA 2K27 was officially released globally on September 4, 2026. Based on Zelnick's comments, GTA 6 won't just have affected NBA 2K27 sales, but caused some gamers to skip other games in favor of Rockstar's next, which comes out November 19. It is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, setting sales and revenue records, so Take-Two will of course be fine for some time to come. Other publishers and developers, though, might be left struggling. For now, though, during the quarter Take-Two saw revenue of $1.6 billion, which was slightly below its guidance range of $1.62-$1.67 billion. The company said fiscal 2027 will be "an historic year for Take-Two – driven by our unwavering commitment to delivering the highest quality entertainment experiences." It reiterated our Fiscal 2027 outlook for revenue of $8-$8.2 billion. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. sources.title: 'The experiences on console and PC tend to be roughly the same,' says Take-Two CEO in response to question about GTA roleplaying
sources.text: Of course, in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, the PC experience at launch will be a blank screen. On a call with investors today , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pushed back on the idea that PC players have a different relationship with the Grand Theft Auto series than console players. "Your PC players seem to engage with GTA a bit differently than console," said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Martin Yang during a Q&A session. "There are roleplay options. Over time, do you think you want to close the player experience gap between console and PC, or do you view the two platforms as more independent because of their respective technical capabilities?" Zelnick responded with acknowledgement that series like Civilization started on PC and expanded onto consoles, but said that "generally speaking, the experiences on console and PC tend to be roughly the same" and that, in general, "the capabilities of the PC platform today aren't different materially from console capabilities." The vanilla GTA Online experience may be roughly equivalent for console and PC players, but the console versions don't have the mods that have helped keep GTA 5 relevant for 13 years. Take-Two of course knows that: It acquired the FiveM GTA 5 multiplayer mod behind so many RP servers. Answering a related question about console jailbreaking, modding, and monetization opportunities, Zelnick said later that "the FiveM business is a profitable business," but then turned back to one of his stock lines. "The mission of this company is to create the best entertainment on earth and bring it to consumers around the world," said the Take-Two CEO. "If we do that right, the monetization takes care of itself." Take-Two has consistently declined to reveal anything about its plans for GTA 6 on PC or the future of GTA Online, and I didn't have high hopes that it would change tack with the console launch just over a week away, but props to the savvy investment analysts who asked about the topics anyway. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. As I think the questioner from Oppenheimer was getting at, it's sensible to wonder whether the custom servers and roleplaying features made popular by GTA 5 modders and streamers on PC will come stock in the next GTA Online iteration, including on consoles. Zelnick didn't sound particularly enthused about modding in his responses today—he said that Take-Two "isn't religious on the topic"—but I'm not reading much into it. For now, Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching on November 19 as a singleplayer-only console game, with no PC release date announced, and no known plans to launch a new version of GTA Online set in Vice City and its surroundings, though we expect both of those things to happen eventually. sources.title: GTA 6 pre-orders are ‘far above initial expectations’ but NBA 2K27 was ‘below our forecast’, Take-Two says
sources.text: NBA was still the second most successful launch in the series’ history, it says Take-Two says pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are “far above initial expectations”, but its other recent major release NBA 2K27 hasn’t met its forecast. Despite delivering “the second highest net bookings performance in the history of the series” and selling more than 4 million copies since its release in early September, NBA 2K27 “was below our forecast for the period”, according to the publisher. It expects big things from GTA 6 , however, stating: “Pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto VI are tracking far above our initial expectations, and we know that the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough.” Despite this claim, Take-Two has only modestly revised its forecast for the financial year, adjusting its range from $7.9 – $8.1 billion up to $7.98 – $8.18 billion. In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company was not yet adjusting its guidance because the game is so close to release. “[We cannot] disclose the numbers, but the point that we’re making is our prior expectations obviously were aligned with our guidance, and the pre-orders are far exceeding our original expectations,” Zelnick said. “We’re maintaining our guidance, because the release is only 10 days away and we’ll know a lot more after the release.” When asked whether the decision to keep the guidance at around $8 billion for the year was a sign that Take-Two wasn’t predicting a bigger than expected launch, Zelnick reiterated: “We’re just not updating our numbers right now because we are so close to the launch. However, pre-orders are far exceeding our expectations.” Elsewhere in the interview, Zelnick was asked whether he felt the wave of live service games had passed. He replied that the vast majority of Take-Two’s income still comes from live service titles (such as GTA Online, NBA 2K or WWE 2K), the upcoming release of GTA aside. “We’ve said all along that free-to-play titles are very challenging, whether that’s in mobile or PC or console,” Zelnick explained. “But live service, I would say that’s too broad a brush, because live services are extremely successful. The bulk of our business is represented by live services and what we call recurrent consumer spend. It’s the vast majority of our business today.” He added: “The business basically runs on live services, punctuated by, we hope, some huge releases.”

sources.title: Take-Two boss isn't worried about GTA 6 players jailbreaking PS5 consoles and modding it
sources.text: FiveM is the go-to resource for such things There aren't many sure bets in video games, but GTA 6 is definitely one of the few you can guarantee will be a big launch. The powers that be looking after Rockstar 's long-awaited sequel are so confident, the prospect of players modding their games to circumvent the studio's paid-for services doesn't scare them whatsoever. Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Take-Two , addressed the issue during a shareholder Q&A. "Our purchase of FiveM reflected our support of certain consumers' desires to engage as a creator with our intellectual property," he says. "We've allowed modding in many of our other games. We're just not religious on the topic. The FiveM business is a profitable business for us." FiveM is a custom multiplayer framework for GTA 5. It has a sibling platform called RedM for Red Dead Redemption 2 , and Rockstar bought out the team behind both in 2023. Other, similar portals have since been shut down because FiveM is essentially the 'official' resource for such things. With GTA 6, there'll likely be a rash of other sites and forums to help people modify the game in some way. They'll piggyback off existing methods of jailbreaking the console. Zelnick isn't phased, because he's aware the crime sandbox is going to bring in plenty of money globally. "The mission of this company is to create the best entertainment on Earth and bring it to consumers around the world," he states. "If we do that right, the monetization takes care of itself, and I think that you're going to see that from us in this fiscal year and in future fiscal years." Whatever the critical consensus of the sixth Grand Theft Auto winds up being, I sincerely doubt anyone involved will need to worry too much about their bottom line, even if a few players manage to duck out of paying for any kind of microtransactions. And it all kicks off in nine days. sources.title: Rockstar Says GTA VI Is ‘Targeting’ 30 FPS And Will Use PSSR On PS5 Pro
sources.text: If you pre-ordered a digital version of GTA VI , you can preload it right now, and considering its massive file-size, getting a nine-day head start on that download might be a good idea. But in addition to announcing the pre-load, Rockstar Games has revealed some extra information on the game’s specifications and features, and a brief but glittery new trailer to accompany the announcement. The biggest thing on the list of specifications is the framerate. Sorry to anyone hoping for a buttery-smooth 60 FPS on console but GTA VI , according to Rockstar, is “targeting 30 frames per second.” That word “targeting” seems especially fraught, suggesting you might not even get all 30 frames all the time. On the PS5 Pro the game will make use of PSSR upscaling and feature ray-tracing while your regular degular PS5 consoles get “high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering […], and improved load times.” Over on the Xbox side of things, you’ll be able to play the game via Xbox Cloud Streaming on the X and S console, and on the Xbox One with Series S graphics. Rockstar warns that trying to stream the game might lead to some technical difficulties. “Connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay,” Rockstar’s announcement reads. “ GTAVI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.” It is not long now, and with this new information, GTA VI feels even closer. sources.title: New GTA 6 trailer showcases PS5-exclusive DualSense features
sources.text: GTA 6 will use haptic feedback and more on PS5 PlayStation has outlined how Grand Theft Auto 6 will make use of the DualSense controller on PS5. In a new trailer, we get a look at some PS5 -exclusive features that will be available in GTA 6. Most of these centre around the DualSense, as Rockstar makes use of the PS5’s unique controller. As the trailer showcases, haptic feedback will kick in for certain activities. Combat is one of them, as it appears that we’ll feel the recoil from weapons in the back triggers, but we also see that there will be additional pressure applied when we’re lifting weights. It also appears that there will be feedback across the entire controller when certain actions happen on screen. An example we’re shown is when the player is thrown by an enemy, likely meaning that the vibrations will kick in differently depending on what happens to us. Lastly, GTA 6 will use the DualSense’s built-in speaker, so we can expect to hear police radio comms coming through the controller. Grand Theft Auto VI is the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history! Mark the occasion with a video showcasing why GTAVI plays best on PS5 Get ready for launch on November 19 by clearing PS5 storage space and pre-loading today: https://t.co/wTPa5E4DJY pic.twitter.com/WTQvHQs9cI While games using these features are nothing new ( Cyberpunk 2077 is another sandbox that used haptic feedback for weaponry, for instance), it certainly looks like Rockstar is trying to squeeze as many unique features out of the DualSense as it can. This lines up with what we’ve heard coming out of Rockstar and PlayStation, with both claiming that GTA 6 will play best on PS5. This is because the two parties agreed to a marketing partnership for GTA 6 , encouraging fans to pick the game up on PS5 as opposed to Xbox Series X/S . With that said, the one thing that Xbox can boast is that it officially has the cheapest way to play GTA 6 at launch. It was confirmed earlier today that we’ll be able to play GTA 6 on Xbox One through cloud streaming, giving us the same performance we would get on Xbox Series S (albeit with the additional performance hits you’d expect from streaming). If you’re looking for the best performance possible, that will be found on PS5 Pro, as that is the only platform that will support ray-tracing. All platforms will target 30 FPS.

sources.text: With no PC port in sight, prospective GTA 6 players need to decide between the PS5 and XBOX Series X|S. Each console has different specs and features to consider. Data shows that GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game ever . The majority are on PS5, but not all of them. Even people who aren’t gamers are jumping at the chance to play GTA 6, which is where the PS5 versus XBOX Series X|S debate comes into play. Also, you can buy Grand Theft Auto 6 here , if you haven’t already! To start, we’re going to run through the respective key default specs for the XBOX Series X model, and the standard PS5 and PS5 Pro variant. The PlayStation 5 Pro is the most powerful current-gen console to play GTA 6 on . For base models, the XBOX Series X|S takes the crown over the normal PS5. However, since the Series X|S doesn’t have a Pro version, the actual overall winner is the PS5 Pro. The Pro has the most powerful hardware and the best features, but it comes with a slight caveat: The price. The base PS5 costs $649.99, whereas you’re looking at $799.99 for the XBOX Series X|S. However, if you want a PS5 Pro, it’ll cost you $899. The RAM Crisis and other operational costs have seen Sony and Microsoft increase console prices instead of the traditional decrease as console lifecycles advance. In my opinion, PlayStation is the best place to enjoy Grand Theft Auto 6, but the debate about the base PS5 and PS5 Pro is a bit tougher where GTA is concerned. If you’re upgrading to current-gen and you only care about having the best GTA 6 experience possible, then it’s recommended you go all out and buy the PS5 Pro. It also means that any subsequent games you buy will be enjoyed best on the console, and the AI-based PSSR (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution) is a juicy graphical improvement for applicable games. sources.title: Rockstar details Grand Theft Auto 6 PS5 Pro enhancements, but it'll still only run at 30FPS
sources.text: Pushing consoles to "their absolute limits". As Grand Theft Auto 6 preloads go live, developer Rockstar has detailed the enhancements coming to the PS5 Pro version of the game, confirming these won't include framerates above the 30 FPS its targeting for consoles. Rockstar shared the news in a blog post released to announce that GTA 6 pre-loading is now available ahead of its release date on 19th November. "Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles," Rockstar says. It goes on to reconfirm GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on all consoles, saying the game is pushing modern machines "to their absolute limits" in order to "bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants." PS5 players can expect high-fidelity haptic feedback through the DualSense controllers, improved spatial audio, and Tempest 3D audio, while PS5 Pro enhancements come in the form of PSSR support and ray tracing shadows, which should make the game look especially fancy, plus improved load times. PlayStation players can also expect remote play support. As for the Xbox, the post clarified details on Xbox Cloud Gaming , which will allow the game to be streamed to Xbox consoles including the Xbox One. Notably, this won't work on PC. Grand Theft Auto 6's 30 FPS target was previously confirmed by Rockstar back in August, but there was some uncertainty around a possible 60fps performance mode at the time. Still, those PS5 technical boons do a lot of work to improve the games it's applied to, which if nothing else should mean GTA 6 will be quite the looker.

sources.text: Sony has just announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become "the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store". On Xbox, meanwhile, cloud streaming is supported , but not - sadly - to PC. sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time I’ve been seeing some chatter online about a specific scene in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time that’s extremely beloved by longtime fans. It’s easy to miss: if you visit the Hyrule Castle Town back alleys after Zelda and Impa flee from Ganondorf, but before the time skip, you can find a soldier on the ground slumped against the wall. In the original, if you speak to him, he asks if you’re the “boy from the forest” and, in a pained stutter, tells you that Ganondorf has betrayed the king and that Zelda has escaped, but that she wanted to give something to you before she left. His final words direct you to the Temple of Time, the text speed slowing as he finishes his line, before he shudders and fully collapses. Trying to speak to him further prompts Navi to say, “He’s not moving anymore….”, and that’s it. The soldier’s dead. This moment has been cited by many as a prime example (among very many!) of the “darkness” of the original Ocarina of Time . It’s an otherwise noble and normal NPC dying a painful death in a back alley due to the cruelty of the villain, in front of the child protagonist who, up to this point, has only seriously fought soulless monsters. He’s not yet had to face down death in this particularly tragic way. In the remake, however, the soldier doesn’t die. He stays alive, and you can talk to him as many times as you like to have him direct you to the Temple of Time. I believe this is just one of a cavalcade of examples of Nintendo being terrified that the player is going to get lost in the remake somehow and not know where to go. What if you forget you’re supposed to go to the Temple? He’s there to remind you, again and again, seemingly merely exhausted instead of in agony. About the soldier in the back alley by u/dampflokfreund in OcarinaOfTime People are bringing this up as evidence that the remake has somehow blunted the “darkness” of the original Ocarina of Time . Defanged it a bit, suggesting a more modern fear from Nintendo of exposing children to grim themes. I saw people say Nintendo “censored” itself here, or that this may have been related to “ratings.” Setting aside questions over whether or not some vague content meter of “darkness” or “maturity” is the measure of anything really, I want to push back on the idea that this moment in Castle Town has been stripped of its power: the soldier lives, yes. But for me, the remake transforms visiting Castle Town between Zelda’s departure and Link’s first experience of time travel in a way that makes it one of the most haunting and sad moments in the entire game…especially if you know what’s coming. When you emerge in Castle Town as Adult Link in either game, it’s in ruins. Dark clouds hover over the square, and Hyrule Castle looms ominously, now the seat of Ganondorf’s power. The once-bustling square is now home to multiple horrifying Redead enemies, heavily implying that some the townsfolk may have been transformed into these health-sucking zombies. You can find most of the major NPCs from Castle Town now living in Kakariko Village, but not all of them make it there. The implication is that Ganondorf essentially enacted a massacre on the town before installing himself as king, and only a handful of refugees escaped to tell the tale. The original Ocarina of Time had some conversationalists in Castle Town right before the timeskip, but many of the NPCs had only a little or even no dialogue, and just served as background to suggest a bustling town square. A few of those characters express some anxiety about the guy on the horse who just galloped through, if you talk to them in the brief window between Zelda’s escape and Link’s transformation. It’s the only time you can hear this special dialogue, but most of it is pretty humdrumâjust folks remarking on the horses that galloped through. The remake’s Castle Town is populated with essentially all of the same NPCs that existed in the original, but with one key difference: just about all of them will speak to you, and most will do so at length, talking about whatever it is that’s on their mind. In that same short window of town panic right after Zelda has fled, almost everyone’s dialogue changes to remark on what just happened…but with a far deeper awareness of what’s coming than was expressed in the original game. A little girl talks about being told to stay away from the “old man chasing people.” The owner of the dog Richard spends all day and night frantically searching for him. Another wealthy woman demands answers from the guards. Some people, happy that fewer people are outside, go on a shopping spree, while one guy ponders stocking up on supplies in case of disaster. Honey and Darling continue to dance blissfully, deliberately ignoring the sound of horses. Multiple NPCs discuss leaving town, aware that an occupation of some sort is imminent. One woman in particular suggests she might move to Goron City, but gives up the idea when she remembers she can’t eat rocks, while another puts her foot down: “Cowardsâall of you! I’m not leaving this town no matter what! I love this place.” When asked what she’ll do if the town is overrun by monsters, she stammers that she’ll “figure it out.” Maybe she’ll make friends with the monsters. Is it weird to say I had to set the controller down for a moment after hearing all this? This whole scene was…a lot. So much more so than it was in the original. I am all-too-aware of many places in real life where people, for years and years, live extremely normal, cheerful lives. Then, something happens. Something off-putting, scary, ominous. Some folks insist everything will be fine. Others panic. Still others double down. And then, the worst thing imaginable, or even something unimaginable. sources.title: Has The Ocarina Of Time Remake Changed Too Much? Fans Debate Difficulty, Tone, And Handholding
sources.text: As is often the case when something is remade, the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is generating a lot of comparisons to the original . Purists will often deride any changes made to the thing they grew up with, so I was prepared for a lot of the discussion to come off like an old man yelling at cloud about how one of the most widely celebrated video games of all time was better âback in his day.â However, the Ocarina of Time remake isnât just getting a lot of the usual remake criticism that tends to revolve around things like graphical fidelity and art style; thereâs also a fair bit of discussion about how its modern game design sensibilities may have sanded off some edges and, in so doing, diminished certain things that made Ocarina of Time great. This morning, I came across a 16-minute video in which Twitter user KloverKlub14 rattled off most of their complaints about the remake. Some of them can be dismissed as nitpicking small details that only the sickest of sickos would ever recognize, but thereâs actually a fair bit here that stood out to me about how much easier Ocarina of Time is on Switch 2 than it ever was on the Nintendo 64. I compiled most of my complaints with the Ocarina remake into this video pic.twitter.com/tnnNx9Jslc — KloverKlub (@KloverKlub14) November 8, 2026 In the flood of complaints, a theme emerges. The difficulty nerf isnât as easy to sum up as saying âLink does more damage than before,â but instead manifests in several little things that add up across the course of the game. Certain environmental hazards are gone, Link no longer lands on a lower floor if he plummets off certain platforms but instead just respawns where he fell from, some enemy behaviors like Stalfos being able to revive themselves if you donât defeat an entire squad of them quickly enough have been removed, and some secrets in the environment are now signposted with elements like dedicated targets for Link to aim the Hookshot at, denying players the pleasure of figuring it out for themselves (or sparing them the effort, depending on how you feel about the change). âPeople keep pointing at better controls and âit was harder for you before because you were a child,â conveniently ignoring that people continued to replay this game into their adulthood,â a redditor writes. âBut it goes beyond that, for both the puzzle and navigation aspect and combat, there are factually things that make it easier. Some dungeon challenges are simplified, objects in the room are less hidden and easier to spot, there’s constant exposition for what you’re supposed to do, challenges that used to be timed now no longer have a timer. Some enemies are easier, some are actually harder, like the Redeads now being more aggressive and able to run. Those changes can be subjective, but there are also changes that objectively make it easier, like Stalfos dealing half the damage they used to. On the other hand, I’ve noticed heart drops are more scarce, and I’ve never seen enemies drop three hearts like they frequently did in the original. Other examples are King Dodongo now being less of a joke, since you can no longer just stand to the side as he rolls past you, and he now also summons baby dodongos. But then there’s bosses like Phantom Ganon who is significantly easier with the slow moving energy balls.â Finished Ocarina remake. Pretty conflicted overall. I think this is a death by a thousand cuts situation honestly. There are too many little things that I loved about the original game that have been lost here. Something Iâve definitely noticed is that some parts of the Ocarina of Time remake feel like theyâre shying away from the darkness of the original game. Yes, I am comparing the level of dread and fear I felt playing the game as a kid to what I feel now as an adult, but Iâm specifically thinking of the original gameâs more explicit references to the violent deaths of people who arenât villains. One notable example that a lot of fans have pointed out is that at the end of the gameâs first act, when Zelda has fled Castle Town and Ganondorf has gone after her, thereâs a soldier who can be found in the back alleys of the town that was originally mortally wounded. The original Ocarina of Time made it pretty clear that he had died from his injuries trying to save Zelda, with the text after his dying words saying âheâs not moving anymore,â but that text no longer appears in the remake. Instead, you can talk to this man as many times as you want. I found the solider! pic.twitter.com/Y0ZUFVlqBB — Steve (@StupidhanyEne) November 5, 2026 Another thing Iâve seen circulating is that some believed blood stains that appeared throughout the Shadow Temple had been removed, as you no longer see the blood-red puddles underneath what look like crucifixes. However, as others have pointed out, old, dried blood wouldnât retain the same crimson color that fresh blood does, so the darker smears that appear in the remake are actually more accurate. I suspect the young development team wanted to bring back the bloodstains in the OoT well, but were probably told no. The result was probably this middle ground of very old stains, just not red. #Zelda pic.twitter.com/SKUsUshcMZ — Mighty (@MightyGazelle1) November 6, 2026 âItâs funny how the more realistic implementation of this with faded dry blood is easier to sneak into an E10 game because it can be passed off as dirt or rust,â a fan writes on Reddit . âThe bright red blood of the OG isâ¦ bloodier, obviously, but arguably more cartoony.â These are smaller details, but thereâs also a pretty major scene in the endgame that no longer includes a character coughing up blood. sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time There’s a new video out from GameXplain showing off differences in how certain locations appear between Breath of The Wild and the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake. The video features side-by-side comparisons of locations shared between the gamesâthe Temple of Time, Lake Hylia, Lon Lon Ranch, and more. And while there’s much to be said for the graphical improvements of Ocarina 4K Electric Boogaloo over BotW , what’s more fascinating is how the similarities reinforce the idea that the worlds of OoT and BotW , separated by different game mechanics and stories and thousands of in-world years, are nevertheless the same. We know, thanks to the Hyrule Hystoria as well as any one of the many attempts by content creators to sort out the Zelda timeline, that Hyrule is one place. That despite the many games with their differing mythologies, including that time the world was totally flooded for like forever , we’ve always been in a singular Hyrule. But this video is perhaps the best illustration of what we’ve always, up to this point, had to take on faith. Look at the Temple of Time. Yes, inÂ Breath of the Wild a whole faÃ§ade of the building has been shorn off by calamity and time, but looking at it, you could believe it’s the same structure that a distant ancestor of Link brought three spiritual stones to when he was little boy. The interiors of the buildings are slightly different, possibly indicating that these aren’t the same assets, but even if so, it’s hardly uncommon for buildings to be remodeled or restored, leaving them slightly changed from what they were. I like the stories these similar but slightlyÂ differentÂ structures tell. Death Mountain stands tall in Ocarina of Time , but has been worn down to a nub in Breath of the Wild . And all that’s left of Lon Lon Ranch by the time Breath of the Wild occurs are a few long-abandoned remnants of the place that Malon and Talon once called home. It’s really neat to see this kind of continuity. The Zelda series has obviously achieved that in other ways, too, like having the same characters pop up over and over, but to see it in the structures themselves is a nice little visual reminder that the worlds of these two very different games are really the same world, changed by time. sources.text: Weeks after the Switch 2 was jailbroken for the first time , Nintendo's latest system update has reportedly patched the exploit that could have allowed users to mod and dump games, putting a stop to those activities… at least for now. The initial jailbreak in question was always limited. Legitimate game-programming app SmileBASIC 4 – which could be downloaded straight from the Switch eShop prior to this whole debacle – could essentially serve as a gateway for exploits that could let folks access parts of the Switch 2 that the average user really isn't meant to reach. There was a catch, though – as a tethered jailbreak, it relied on the software and on it staying open – if you were to turn your system off, you'd have to repeat the entire jailbreak process when you turned it back on. Even so, hackers were still able to use this to dump Switch 2 games and their assets, as well as mod games like Mario Kart World – in fact, one of the jailbreak's first documented uses was putting Hatsune Miku, Peter Griffin, and Sanrio character Cinnamoroll into Nintendo's racing game. Now, though, according to modder and dataminer OatmealDome, that should no longer be the case thanks to Switch 2 system update 23.5.0, which rolled out a few hours ago. "The OS exploit used in the recent jailbreak has been patched in version 23.5.0," OatmealDome writes on Twitter. "Dumping and modding games will be impossible again from this point forward, with the exception of some cartridge games (and maybe game updates) that are released in the near future." They report that game exploits, like the aforementioned SmileBASIC 4 one as well as an exploit tied to physical copies of Civilization 7, still exist, but "it is no longer possible to 'escape' the game starting with 23.5.0. This effectively means that the capabilities of homebrew are locked to whatever the game can do already (i.e. not much)." There's no doubt that as far as Nintendo is concerned, this patch couldn't come soon enough. Mere hours after the release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, the game was running on PC after being dumped from a Switch 2 copy , which I can't imagine the house of Mario was particularly pleased about. Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+. But the question is, is Pandora's box now open? With exploits and the like, we often tend to see that striking down one thing just leads to another three appearing – just look at the literal thousands of clones of Switch emulator Yuzu that surfaced after Nintendo took down the original . Some have also claimed that this update may not be as effective as you might think. According to Twitter account SwitchTools , it'll still be possible to dump new physical games on this firmware – though Game Key Cards will be immune. "Digital games, updates, and DLC cannot be downloaded and dumped without [Nintendo Switch Online]," they say. Beyond that, multiple users online are expressing that they'll not be updating their system in order to keep access to the exploit, so it may not have been a perfect fix for Nintendo regardless. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake win proves price hike isn’t slowing momentum, Nintendo president says
sources.text: The latest Zelda game is "off to a great start," says Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa Nintendo says The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is "off to a great start" and the 40th Anniversary Edition Switch 2 console has also been "very positive," heading off speculation from an investor that price hikes may be hurting momentum. Taking questions as part of its latest financial briefing , Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa is pressed on how well the Switch 2 is selling its wares after the console's price jumped to $500 earlier this year. Investors reckon things are slowing down, and they don't like that. As such, one asks the Nintendo suits whether they think current financial goals will still be met. The short answer is absolutely; just look at how well Zelda's Ocarina of Time remake and 40th-anniversary console are doing. "Adoption has progressed smoothly over the roughly one and a half years since Nintendo Switch 2 launched last June, and the installed base now exceeds 25 million units," Furukawa says. "At the end of last year's holiday season, we explained that there were regional differences in how well our expectations were met. But the March release of Pokemon Pokopia acted as a driver of global hardware sales, and we entered the new fiscal year with good momentum." Furukawa continues by saying that, while the Switch 2 did indeed increase in price, the impact hasn't been too great because most people were given plenty of notice and have had plenty of hardware and software bundles to compensate for it. That takes us to today, where Nintendo is seemingly riding high thanks to all things Zelda. Furukawa says the special version of the Switch 2 designed to celebrate Zelda's 40th anniversary has been "very positive" for the company and has "contributed to strong sales in various regions." Meanwhile, while it's too early to delve too far into the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake numbers, Furukawa says it's "off to a great start," and that Nintendo is in "good shape for the coming holiday season," too. "Holiday season sales significantly impact the number of units shipped annually for our dedicated video game platform business," he says. "Given the hardware price revisions, we think the sales trends over the next several weeks will be key to achieving our sales guidance." Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week While no official numbers are given, there are signs that, yeah, those Zelda products are shifting units. As per Circana, the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 drove record sales for Nintendo in the US. In fact, it was only last month that a Nintendo exec said those at the house of Mario "underestimated" how well it would sell. Stock has been an issue, though a welcome one. We have less to go on with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. That said, analyst firms say the N64 throwback is the largest physical launch in the UK so far this year. With the festive period coming up, I can see why Nintendo isn't sweating this one too hard right now. sources.title: How to get the Scarecrow Song in Ocarina of Time
sources.text: Dancing through life, swaying and sweeping In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, the Scarecrow Song is an optional but useful song you can unlock to help you get to otherwise impossible to reach places. You don't need the song to beat the game, but you will need it to get every Piece of Heart and Skulltula Token . The song allows you to summon a scarecrow to a set location, allowing you to use your Hookshot to jump over to it. Nifty! Below, we explain how to unlock the Scarecrow Song in the Ocarina of Time remake . As young Link, talk to the scarecrows at Lake Hylia. They're right at the entrance on the farmed land. Pierre, the one closer to the entrance of the lake, will tell you to come up with a song yourself using your ocarina. Note that whatever you play here will become the Scarecrow Song . Feel free to be creative, but keep in mind that every time you play the Scarecrow Song, you'll have to watch Link play it out as you play it here. This means if you drag the song out to be very long, you'll get a long cutscene each time. Memorize whatever you play here, take a screenshot of it, or write it down, as the game will not record it anywhere for you (yet). Talk to Bonooru, the second scarecrow, and play the song for him. He'll love it! Now head to the Temple of Time after completing the Forest Temple , or by playing the Prelude of Light. Allow yourself to turn into adult Link by drawing out the Master Sword and return to Lake Hylia . You'll notice that Pierre isn't there anymore, but Bonooru is! Talk to Bonooru, and he'll ask you to play the Scarecrow Song you wrote again. Play the song , he'll happily dance around, and a familiar face will pop out of the ground: Pierre! He'll be so thrilled with your playing that he'll note that if you see any hay flowing around in the wind , you can play the song, and he'll pop up for you there. The Scarecrow Song will also be saved in the top right slot when you press ZL with your ocarina out, so you don't have to memorize it anymore. Notably, there's a place right in front of Bonooru that has this swirl, in front of the old fishing lodge. Feel free to test out your new song there. You can head up and earn the Golden Scale from the fishing lodge and reach other collectibles around Hyrule. There's also a swirling hay tornado on the roof of the laboratory, which will let you bypass the magic bean requirement to grab the Piece of Heart on top of the tower. If you forgot what song you taught the scarecrows as young Link, you can go back to Lake Hylia as a child and Bonooru will play it for you again. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a little bit different than the original game, so if you need guides to help you through, we don’t blame you. We have walkthroughs for all the dungeons, from the Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Castle . We also have guides for the sillier, in-between parts of the game, like when you have to find Richard (the dog) or Cuccos . For those going for 100% completion, we also have guides on where to find every Piece of Heart , every Gold Skulltula token , and where to plant every Magic Bean .

sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's High-Quality Visuals Have Players Second-Guessing Decades of Memories
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gives Link's first 3D adventure a new coat of paint, but some of its details have players second-guessing the reality they thought they once knew. You don't have to be a Zelda expert to know what fairies look like in the original Ocarina of Time. Navi is an icon, which means most people who have ever even thought about touching one of the games in Nintendo's beloved fantasy franchise know that Link's little guide is little more than a glowing ball with wings – or so they thought. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought more than just a fancy new tunic for Link when it made the leap to Switch 2 last week. A few close-up shots early in the adventure make one shocking fact clear: The fairies of Kokiri Forest aren't orbs of light – they're fuzzy . It's the kind of detail the original Nintendo 64 release could have never conveyed made real thanks to the artists at Nintendo and the power of the Switch 2. It's about as small as details come but also recontextualizes how many – myself included – have viewed Ocarina of Time's fairies for the last 28 years. "It appears Fairies are just...Fluffy Balls that emit a light!" one Reddit user said . "It's neither a ball of pure light or a humanoid lil person hidden under a glow. Just...Fluff! Interesting :D And cute!" "Answering the important lore questions like 'is that a sentient puffball or a tiny lady who's so shiny you can only see her aura,'" another fan commented . Zelda lore is packed with details that fans have obsessed over for decades, so a revelation like this is kind of groundbreaking. Was it always Nintendo's intention for the fairies to be tiny talking puffballs? Probably not, and if you prefer the pure light orb fairies they'll always be there, too, but fans at least seem to have taken to the change after weekend one. @TAHK0 This is the best thing that’s ever happened to me Fairies are far from the only characters making players question their childhood memories. One that more people have realized pre-remake has to do with the attire of Hyrule guards. Don't worry, if it looked to you like they were wearing some pretty standard fantasy knight armor, you'll be happy to know that is exactly what they're wearing in 2026. "He's wearing f**king jorts?????" one player questioned . "Yes and he looks great in it," another replied . So far my favorite part of the Ocarina of Time Remake is that the guards are wearing booty jorts https://t.co/kjj8kYzORf "I like to believe that all the guards are forced to wear jorts under penalty of death, purely because Zelda decrees it so," another Reddit user suggested . "It’s a really nice detail they added in the remake." Unlike the fairies, it does seem like jorts were standard issue for Zelda's royal guard back in the day. It's just that it's easier to tell that now thanks to the Ocarina of Time remake's Switch 2 graphics. It's made for some funny reactions online, but not all of the new details are quite as charming as jort-wearing knights. Boundary Break host Shesez, who offers out-of-bounds perspectives on video games, got up close and personal with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's creepiest enemies: the ReDeads. In the N64 game, these mummified zombie grapplers were scary enough thanks to their empty eye sockets. On Switch 2, they still look eyeless – at least at a first glance. Get close (but not too close) enough for a good look, zoom in, and you'll see the developers were nice enough to give ReDead's soulless eyeballs behind their masks. Thanks, Nintendo! "That's 100% human skull behind that mask," one person said . The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launched last week for Switch 2 and has been picked apart (complimentary) by the internet in just a few days. Dataminers have found potential hints for what could be some exciting new content . Speedrunners have found some game-changing glitches that have produced some hilarious results . Meanwhile, as players get used to their new jump button, Link is going through it . sources.title: The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake já roda a 60 FPS e ganha até multiplayer no PC
sources.text: O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, lançado recentemente para Nintendo Switch 2, já está sendo executado em computadores por meio de emuladores. Poucas horas depois da estreia oficial, usuários conseguiram inicializar o jogo no PC, embora a experiência inicial fosse marcada por problemas gráficos, travamentos e desempenho instável. A situação, no entanto, mudou rapidamente. Apenas um dia depois das primeiras tentativas, atualizações dos emuladores Lichii e Eglantine já permitem executar o clássico da Nintendo a até 60 quadros por segundo (FPS), com melhorias significativas na qualidade visual e na estabilidade. Além disso, modders também já trabalham para trazer suporte para multiplayer ao game nos computadores. Até o momento, a Nintendo não comentou sobre o assunto, mas a situação pode levar a movimentações legais da companhia. De acordo com informações do DSOGaming , o emulador Lichii conseguiu corrigir boa parte dos problemas gráficos identificados no primeiro dia de testes. Regiões como a área inicial do jogo e a Árvore Deku já podem ser executadas a 60 FPS, contra os 20 a 30 FPS registrados nas primeiras tentativas. Relatos publicados por usuários também apontam resultados ainda melhores em algumas configurações. Um jogador afirmou ter conseguido executar o remake em 4K e 60 FPS estáveis, sem os principais problemas visuais observados anteriormente, embora pequenos travamentos e congelamentos ainda aconteçam. Outro teste, compartilhado na comunidade do emulador Eglantine, utilizou um processador Ryzen 7 5700X e uma placa de vídeo RTX 5070. O jogador conseguiu avançar até a obtenção da Espada Kokiri em um novo arquivo, mas ainda encontrou problemas de cintilação de texturas, iluminação e dessincronização de áudio em determinadas cenas. Parte da evolução aconteceu graças a mudanças específicas no funcionamento dos emuladores. O Lichii, que é baseado no Eglantine, recebeu correções para problemas que provocavam flashes brancos na tela, cenas completamente pretas e falhas na exibição da vegetação. Os desenvolvedores também trabalharam em otimizações de desempenho, incluindo melhorias no carregamento e armazenamento de shaders. Entre as mudanças estão o reaproveitamento de pipelines gráficos já compilados e a execução de determinadas tarefas em segundo plano durante a inicialização do jogo. O repositório do Eglantine mostra que a equipe publicou diferentes versões experimentais voltadas especificamente à compatibilidade com Ocarina of Time. Como resultado, o progresso tem sido bastante rápido, embora ainda existam limitações que podem variar conforme o hardware e a versão utilizada. Além de melhorar o desempenho do remake no PC, a comunidade de modders já começou a trabalhar em outro recurso: um modo multiplayer. Um vídeo publicado nesta segunda-feira (9) mostra uma versão preliminar da modificação em funcionamento no emulador Lichii, permitindo que jogadores compartilhem a aventura no clássico da Nintendo. O projeto ainda está em desenvolvimento e não possui previsão de lançamento. A expectativa é que a modificação também seja compatível com a versão não oficial do jogo para PC, embora isso ainda dependa de testes e ajustes dos responsáveis pelo projeto. O remake também chamou atenção por uma demonstração envolvendo tecnologias de upscaling. O canal ElAnalistaDeBits publicou uma comparação mostrando como o NVIDIA DLSS pode melhorar a qualidade da imagem do jogo em relação ao AMD FSR 1.0 utilizado originalmente. A demonstração utiliza uma técnica de injeção de DLSS via HDMI, em vez de alterar diretamente o funcionamento interno do jogo. Na comparação, a tecnologia da NVIDIA reduz efeitos de cintilação e melhora a definição de elementos da imagem. Vale lembrar que o Nintendo Switch 2 possui suporte ao DLSS, tecnologia que também já aparece em jogos de outras desenvolvedoras para o console. Mesmo assim, a Nintendo optou pelo FSR 1.0 em Ocarina of Time, uma escolha que chamou atenção diante das possibilidades oferecidas pelo hardware. A chegada do remake aos computadores com modificações também acontece em meio a uma nova onda de avanços na comunidade de emulação do Switch 2. Segundo os relatos, os arquivos do jogo começaram a circular antes do lançamento, após cópias físicas chegarem antecipadamente a alguns consumidores. The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake vale a pena no Switch 2? Confira análise do jogo A extração dos arquivos estaria relacionada ao ns2jb, ferramenta de desbloqueio do console que se tornou pública recentemente. Pouco depois da divulgação do método, outros jogos exclusivos, como Mario Kart World, também começaram a inicializar em emuladores para PC e até mesmo em dispositivos da Apple. A Nintendo não comentou oficialmente sobre o caso, mas já estaria tomando medidas contra possíveis brechas utilizadas nesse processo. O aplicativo SmileBASIC 4, apontado como uma das portas de entrada para a exploração do sistema, foi removido da eShop. No passado, a empresa também tomou medidas legais contra desenvolvedores de emuladores em uma situação parecida. Após arquivos de Zelda Tears of the Kingdom vazarem antes do lançamento, a companhia iniciou movimentações contra o Yuzu em 2024 por pirataria . Logo, não seria surpreendente ver novas medidas contra ferramentas como Lichii e Eglantine. Em seu site, a Nintendo também deixa claro que é contra o uso de emuladores. A empresa vê os softwares como prejudiciais ao seu modelo de negócio. “Os emuladores não autorizados permitem que certos jogos sejam utilizados de formas não previstas originalmente pelos criadores e incentivam a utilização de cópias não autorizadas (ou seja, pirateadas) dos jogos”, diz a empresa. “Logo, os emuladores têm um impacto negativo na experiência de jogo dos usuários, nos investimentos realizados pelos criadores para desenvolver e publicar jogos únicos e inovadores e, assim, na indústria dos videogames em geral.” E aí, qual a sua opinião sobre o assunto? The pair formed DC Studios in 2022, and kicked off a new movie continuity for DC heroes with last year’s acclaimedÂ Superman . This year’sÂ Supergirl was not quite as well received and performed poorly at the box office .Â Clayface , a body horror film about the Batman villain of the same name, was released last month. On the TV side,Â Lanterns and Peacemaker were both received very well after debuting on HBO Max, though the DC Universe’s choices for some early projects had drawn a fair bit of criticism for focusing on obscure characters instead of major players like Batman and Wonder Woman. The People v. Gorilla GroddÂ is an upcoming mockumentary series starring Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olson after he debuted as the comic relief character in Superman . Gunn is still attached to next year’sÂ Man of Tomorrow , which he wrote and directed, but both he and Safran “will return full time to creative work” after years of overseeing the DCU’s direction. Update, 11/9/26, 1:15 p.m. Eastern:Â Gunn has released a statement on his Instagram account, confirming he is still working with DC on bothÂ Man of Tomorrow and another project he’s writing on. He leaves it open-ended on whether or not he’ll continue working with the company, saying “we’ll see where it goes after that.” Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios. When I was a kid growing up in Manchester, Missouri, I used to write and draw my own comics with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters. Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn’t know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn’t pass up the unique opportunity. I’m glad I took the job. There have been so many highs along the way – releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to The People Vs, the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments. The highest of the highs have been all the talented and wonderful people I’ve worked with and grown to love: the DC Studios crew, our talented collaborators, our casts and crews, and the boisterous and hilarious fans. And the best part of all has been working with Peter Safran, the smartest and most competent person I know. You’ve been the best partner a person could ask for, and, more so, a truly good friend. But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years (Jenn, I love you and I’m sorry and you don’t need to feel guilty for being the happiest of all people that I’m no longer doing this job). sources.text: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-heads of DC Studios and will be replaced by former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham James Gunn and DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran are stepping down as the heads of DC Studios and will be replaced by former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham. Per The Hollywood Reporter , Gunn and Safran are out of the job from December 1, 2026. That's just over four years after the pair were appointed to the post. In that time, DC Studios has released three movies ( Superman , Supergirl and Clayface ) and four TV shows (Creature Commandos, Peacemaker season 2 , The Penguin and Lanterns ). Projects currently in the pipeline include Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow , Jimmy Olsen series The People v. Gorilla Grodd, Creature Commandos season 2, and Elseworlds movie The Batman: Part II . “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision," Gunn and Safran said in a statement. "In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker, Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. "We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. "We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter," Gunn and Safran said of their replacement at DC Studios. "We're excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow." In a separate, longer statement on Threads , Gunn said he's "incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking" and noted "the characters we set up will live on". Latcham is Marvel Studios' former senior VP of production and development, and was Kevin Feige's right-hand man at the company for a time, with credits on Iron Man, The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy and Spider-Man: Homecoming. As with Gunn and Safran, Latcham will oversee DC's film, TV and animation slate. "James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of," Skydance bosses David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz said in a statement . "We're grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand." Subscribe for a weekly digest of the movie and TV news that matters, direct to your inbox. From first-look trailers, interviews, reviews and explainers, we’ve got you covered. What the future now holds for DC is now less clear than ever. While several projects from the Gunn and Safran era are still in the pipeline, many were critical of Gunn and Safran's decision not to launch their shared universe with big-hitters like Batman and Wonder Woman, and instead focus on lesser-explored characters like Supergirl and Clayface. Could a creative reboot be on the cards, despite Gunn's Superman movies still being an ongoing concern? We'll soon find out. Man of Tomorrow releases on July 9, 2027.
